context.title: Born in Bethlehem
context.summary: A census brings Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem, where Jesus is born and laid in a manger. Angels announce him to shepherds. At the temple Simeon and Anna recognize him, and at twelve Jesus amazes the teachers.
context.background: Luke ties the birth to a census under Caesar Augustus while Cyrenius (Quirinius) governed Syria. Quirinius' best-known census was in AD 6, after Herod's death, so scholars debate how to fit Luke's dating together.

customs.note: A manger was a feeding trough for animals. Newborns were wrapped snugly in strips of cloth, a normal sign of care.
After childbirth a mother brought a lamb and a bird for purification, but a family that could not afford a lamb could bring two birds (Leviticus 12:8).

watchFor: The good news is 'to all people' (v. 10), and Simeon calls Jesus a light to the Gentiles (v. 32).
Mary 'kept' these things and 'pondered them in her heart' (vv. 19, 51).

people.name: Augustus
people.summary: The cognomen of the first Roman emperor, C. Julius Caesar Octavianus, during whose reign Christ was born (Luke 2:1). His decree that “all the world should be taxed” was the divinely ordered occasion of Jesus’ being born, according to prophecy (Micah 5:2), in Bethlehem.

people.name: Cyrenius
people.summary: The Grecized form of Quirinus. His full name was Publius Sulpicius Quirinus. Recent historical investigation has proved that Quirinus was governor of Cilicia, which was annexed to Syria at the time of our Lord’s birth.

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: The foster-father of our Lord (Matt. 1:16; Luke 3:23). He lived at Nazareth in Galilee (Luke 2:4). He is called a “just man.”

people.name: Mary
people.summary: The wife of Joseph, the mother of Jesus, called the “Virgin Mary,” though never so designated in Scripture (Matt. 2:11; Acts 1:14). Little is known of her personal history.

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: Asher
people.summary: Happy, Jacob’s eigth son; his mother was Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid (Gen. 30:13). Of the tribe founded by him nothing is recorded beyond its holding a place in the list of the tribes (35:26; 46:17; Ex. 1:4, etc.) It increased in numbers twenty-nine percent, during the thirty-eight years’ wanderings.

people.name: Anna
people.summary: Grace, an aged widow, the daughter of Phanuel. She was a “prophetess,” like Miriam, Deborah, and Huldah (2 Chr. 34:22). After seven years of married life her husband died, and during her long widowhood she daily attended the temple services.

people.name: Phanuel
people.summary: Face of God, father of the prophetess Anna, Luke 2:36.

places.name: Syria
places.summary: (Heb. Aram), the name in the Old Testament given to the whole country which lay to the north-east of Phoenicia, extending to beyond the Euphrates and the Tigris.

places.name: Bethlehem
places.summary: A city in the “hill country” of Judah. It was originally called Ephrath (Gen. 35:16, 19; 48:7; Ruth 4:11). It was also called Beth-lehem Ephratah (Micah 5:2), Beth-lehem-judah (1 Sam. 17:12), and “the city of David” (Luke 2:4).

places.name: Galilee
places.summary: Circuit. Solomon rewarded Hiram for certain services rendered him by the gift of an upland plain among the mountains of Naphtali. Hiram was dissatisfied with the gift, and called it “the land of Cabul”.

places.name: Judea
places.summary: After the Captivity this name was applied to the whole of the country west of the Jordan (Hag. 1:1, 14; 2:2).

places.name: Nazareth
places.summary: Separated, generally supposed to be the Greek form of the Hebrew netser, a “shoot” or “sprout.”

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).
